title: Stephen Dedalus,
html_source:
Stephen Dedalus is, to put it very bluntly and broadly, Joyce’s artistic representation of his self. He is the protagonist of Joyce’s previous novel, A Portrait of The Artist as a Young Man, a bildungsroman which draws heavily on Joyce’s own formative experiences.

In Stephen Hero, an early version of what became Portrait, Stephen’s surname is spelled “Daedalus” in more precise allusion to Daedalus, the architect in Greek myth who was contracted by King Minos to build the Labyrinth in which he would imprison his wife’s son the Minotaur.

Stephen appears in Ulysses as the character who correlates to Telemachus. He harnesses, tentatively, aspects of Hamlet. He is the protagonist of the first three chapters.

More fancifully, we might view Stephen as an autobiographical reference for the being who builds the labyrinth (Ulysses the novel) for King Minos (Joyce himself?) to imprison an unconquerable beast– what the beast is would require an overreaching level of speculation.
